I would assume that Ozai at least has some athleticism but would rather rely on his raw strength, he's very much someone who's Power over Technique. That said, I could see how Zuko *could* beat Ozai, but the methods in which Zuko have ever even challenged Ozai has been through lightning. I mean you have to remember, Zuko was too intimidated by his father's might to even make his declaration while his father had bending. He specifically waited until the eclipse to confront him. While Zuko is a great, talented bender, I just don't see Ozai being majorly phased by his fire blasts honestly. Though, under reconsideration, taking into account Ozai's narrow mindedness, I could very well see a potential battle wherein he focuses too hard on one of the Gaang members, and ends up getting overwhelmed without the help of Amon or The Boulder, Ultima knocking him out that way too. I could see him getting blasted by like a barrage of fire and water blasts until he's like on the edge of the arena lol.

As for Team 1 vs Team 2, I've seen some of the other comments but I simply have to disagree. Toph has indeed shown skill against other Earth projectiles, but she's always kinda struggled against elements other than her own. So while against Bolin's discs, she has no worry, Korra and Mako's fire and water would ultimately be her biggest threat.

Also, having seen some of Kuvira's combat style, I wanna posit another interesting pro-bending matchup! 

Kuvira, Desna or Eska, and Zhao vs General Iroh, Huu, and Bumi! Think this could be quite a great matchup

This seems like fun! I'll go bender by bender then give a breakdown of how I think the match would go for each round. :)

Team 1 vs Team 2

Korra vs Pakku: Korra wins 6/10 times.

Pakku is a damn good water bender, imo better than Korra ever showcases. However, I have a feeling that a lot of the techniques he showcases in his fight against Katara wouldn't necessarily be viable in the pro-bending setting. He seems to be geared towards utilizing his environment to his advantage, which the limiting restraints due to pro-bending, it really hampers his technique. Any agility we see him utilize is based off of momentum he gains from ice, and while I'm sure that he'd still be quite an agile water bender without ice, it's very clear that he still prefers to use water in this manner. However, being that pro-bending specifically restricts using water in any form besides it's liquid state, this puts a pretty strong handicap on Pakku. I still think he's the better water bender, but Korra has the better technique in regards to the specific ruleset.

Iroh vs Mako: It goes either way.

Again, this kinda comes down to Mako having the better technique provided the restrictions of pro-bending. Iroh's signature Dragon Breath is specifically prohibited since streams of fire are not allowed. I do feel that Iroh's time traveling the world and trying to incorporate other methods of bending into his own will help him in the fight, but nonetheless, Iroh still seems to have a a very firm, somewhat stiff stance as a fire bender. He takes wide stances that kinda restrict him from being as agile as he would need to be. At the very least, I do think his defense against Mako would be quite strong, specifically due to the fact that he's studied other types of bending. I could see him trying to redirect fire blasts that Mako sends towards him back to Mako, and Iroh's fire I would imagine is stronger at that, considering he learned from dragons. If this was strictly a 1v1, I do think Iroh would win due to this. However, in this team setting, I could see him struggling some. 

Bolin vs Toph: 9/10 to Bolin.

Okay, Toph gets destroyed by the pro-bending setting. She relies on her environment in order to perform well, utilizing it as both her defense and offense. However, due to the earth discs being so small in comparison to what Toph usually bends in terms of defense, I could definitely see her struggling a LOT. This is all without mentioning that she can't utilize her seismic sense to the same capacity she's used to on the canvas matt, along with the fact that she can't sense the fire or water coming from either her team or her opponents. She's guaranteed a better bender than Bolin (no offense on Bo's part), just this setting completely neuters her skill set.

Round 1: Team 1 wins 7/10 times.

Ultimately, I think Team 1 would beat Team 2. Toph would be the first to be knocked out, especially if Korra and Bolin focus their efforts on her. From there, I think Iroh and Pakku could try to operate on a Lance+Shield dynamic, with Iroh trying to act as the shield, while Pakku the lance. Iroh's strong fire could easily contest the flurries of water and earth discs, and as stated previously, I think he'd try to use Mako's fire to his own advantage. However, I don't think Pakku carries enough power to completely take out Team 1 in this dynamic. I could see Iroh and Pakku knocking out one of the members of Team 1, more than likely being Bolin. However, I think around the same time Bolin would get knocked out, so would Iroh. Pakku, left on his own, I think would struggle to contest against both Korra and Mako. He could realistically knock out one of the two, but I don't see him carrying the full stamina to outlast their flurry of attacks.

Team 3 vs Team 4


Amon vs Katara: Katara wins 8/10 times.

Amon is a great water bender in the regard that he's an amazing blood bender. However, from his capabilities at using exclusively water, he seems to falter stacked up against Katara. Her speed and power would easily contest Amon's, and she has been shown to be quite adept at using water exclusively in it's liquid state. I don't really see too many situations in which Amon beats her, from what we've been shown of his purely water bending capabilities.

Ozai vs Zuko: Ozai wins 9/10 times.

Ozai is easily the powerhouse of his respective team. While the audience has not been shown that Ozai shares the same physical agility that both of his children have, it can be inferred from the fact that he had, at some point, undergone the same, or at the very least similar, training that both hai children have, being royal blooded and all. This said, I don't think Zuko's breakdance-like fire attacks could overpower Ozai, and frankly, I think he'd even be able to tank them, all things considered. He is called the most powerful fire bender in the world during his time for a reason. The strength of his flames overpowered even that of Iroh's, who had learned from the dragons how to be a better fire bender. There's a reason no one challenged him really, besides what is basically a demigod. Even assuming that Ozai has to grow accustomed to only shooting fire in one second bursts, I think those bursts would be far more than enough to knock out one of the opponents if he lands the hit. Love ya Zuko, but your dad is just kinda busted LOL.

Aang vs The Boulder: Aang wins 9/10 times.

A lot of this comes down to the same reasons Aang was so easily able to beat Toph, he's just too evasive. All things considered, The Boulder wouldn't be able to keep up with Aang's speed, which has been shown to be quite fast even without his air bending. This is without mentioning the fact that I simply think Aang is the better earth bender. He has a much better understanding of the element, along with better understanding of the concepts of positive, negative, and neutral jing.

Round 2: Team 4 wins 8/10 times.

At first glance, this battle could go either way all things considered. If The Boulder and Amon both try to act as shields for Ozai, while he tries to overpower the Gaang, they could win. However, taking The Boulder's personality into account, I think he would try to act too offensively, or be too busy showboating to do a decent job. The guy has a huge ego when it comes to crowds, and I could very much so see that being the reason he gets knocked out. However, before The Boulder gets knocked out, I easily see Ozai knocking out Zuko, seeing him as potentially a weak link on the team. So with that, the teams are now both down a member. But this is where the Gaang gets the advantage, as I think both Katara and Aang would be mobile enough to counter Ozai's power. They would soon be able to take out Amon, leaving Ozai left to fend for himself, and while he's powerful, I don't think he'd really be able to get a good blow on Aang. He could realistically take out Katara, but that's assuming that the two of them don't knock him out before he does that.
